text.p: Texaco Inc expects further increases in the employment of minorities and women over the next four years as a result of a plan adopted to ensure fairness and economic opportunity for its employees and business partners, the company said Wednesday.

Noting minority employement has increased to 23 percent from 16 percent in 1991, Texaco said "the company expects it will reach a level of 29 percent by the end of the year 2000. Also by that time, Texaco expects that its African American employment will increase from nine percent to 13 percent ... and employment of women from 32 percent to 35 percent.
"These increases will take place in the context of modest overall employment growth during this period," Texaco said.
Development of the diversity plan follows the company's review of its human resources and busines partnering programs "undertaken as a result of events over the past six weeks."

"Based on our review, we have set ... initiatives that are well balanced and beneficial to all our employees and bring us a critical competitive advantage," chief executive Peter I. Bijur said. "The goals of our program were set by determining what the demographics of Texaco's workforce are likely to be in the year 2000."
"And, to be clear, these are goals -- they are not quotas," Bijur said.
Texaco said it will track the progress of all of the new and enhanced programs and report on these efforts
To help achieve its goal of attracting and retaining a highly capable workforce, Texaco said it will in 1997:
-- Enhance the interviewing, selection and hiring skills of its managers;
-- Expand its overall college recruitment;
-- Use search firms with a record of recruiting from a wide, diverse range with key competencies for Texaco; and
-- Establish a mentoring process that will link managers and senior professionals with aspiring employees; and
-- Enhance its global succession planning system.
"The company expects these and other efforts to allow it to increase women and minorities among its managers by more than 25 percent over the next four years," it said.
Texaco said it "will launch several programs by mid-1997 that will enhance the efficiency of its team based approach and, as a result, help reduce cycle times and improve productivity."
The company said it will seek to:
-- Implement a redesigned diversity learning experience, started last year for managers, to include all U.S. employees;
-- Include women and minorities on all Human Resource Committees throughout the company;
-- Introduce a learning program to support all managers with improved skill and knowledge in change management; and
-- Implement Alternative Dispute Resolution including mediation and arbitration, and introduce an ombuds program in which employees may use a confidential outside counselor.
Texaco will continue to hold all employees, especially managers, responsible for these programs, it said.
The company said it will establish reporting structures to increase accountability and also will:
-- Expand the company's 360-degree feedback process for 1997 to include all managers and supervisors;
-- Revise further its evaluations to more closely link managers' compensation to their performance in creating openness in the workplace; and
-- Redesign the employee opinion survey, to be conducted annually beginning in 1997, to help monitor the change.
Texaco said its goal is to increase annual purchases from minority and women owned businesses to more than $1 billion.

This would be up from $135 million in 1996 over five years, with the expectation that it will reach at least six percent of purchases. To broaden its financial relationships, it will seek to raise activities with minority and women-owned banks and money managers to $200 million from $32 million.
Texaco said it is already increasing the number of women and minority banks with which it does business to 50 from 21 and increasing deposits in those banks.
The company said it seeks more women and minority pension fund managers and the funds under their management will rise to $186 million from $31 million, or 13 percent of its funds.
Texaco also said it intends to invest $10 million in 1997 in a minority-managed domestic emerging market fund.
It will increase insurance coverage from minority- and women owned companies to $200 million from $25 million.
The company said it will accelerate efforts to diversify wholesalers/retailers in key markets.
Texaco said its goal is to double the number of minority- and women-owned wholesaler marketers or jobbers from 43 to 85 (from 5.5 percent to over 11 percent) within five years.
The company also plans to encourage these jobbers to maintain the level of minority and women retail operators.
Texaco will work to maintain women and minority independent retail owner and lessee operators at the current level of at least 45 percent of retail outlets.
Within five years, it will work to more than triple African American-owned retail outlets to 117 from 35 (to six percent from two percent of the total).

Texaco will work to maintain its current level of at least 70 percent of minority and women managers at company owned and operated retail outlets and will seek to increase minority retail and store managers to 100 from 67 (to 12 percent from 7.4 percent of the total).

Texaco said it will strive to double the number of minority- and women- owned lubricant distributors to 58 from 29 (to nine percent from 4.5 percent of the total), and to double the number of lube outlets to 104 from 52 (to 17 percent from 8.7 percent of the total).
